generation.mechanism: At elevated temperatures, the thermal energy overcomes the energy barrier for partial dislocation recombination and cross-slip, while lattice distortion effects (sluggish diffusion) fail to stabilize the dislocation structures. This prevents the formation of coherent, protective oxide films (like the stable oxides seen in AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 at 900°C) and instead creates rough, inhomogeneous oxide layers that are continuously removed, similar to the mechanism described for AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 between RT and 500°C but accelerated by thermal lattice softening.
